Outcome.description:
Normalised result of one test execution.

JUnit XML distinguishes a *failure* (an assertion did not hold) from an *error* (the test
could not run to its assertion, e.g. an exception in set-up). Both count as "not passed";
they stay separate because they usually need different people to act.
Outcome.title: Outcome

PipelineJob.description:
The CI pipeline execution and job a run came from (docs/pipelines.md).

One pipeline execution (a GitHub Actions run, a GitLab pipeline, a Jenkins build) usually
has several jobs, and each job writes its own result files. Grouping them is what lets a
gate refuse to decide on a pipeline whose jobs did not all report.

Attributes:
    pipeline_id: Identifier of the pipeline execution (e.g. ``github.run_id``).
    job: Name of the job within the pipeline (``api``, ``ui-chrome``).
    attempt: Re-run number of the job; the highest attempt of a job replaces earlier ones.
    branch: Branch the pipeline ran on, if known.
    commit: Commit the pipeline tested, if known.
    repository: The repository whose pipeline it is (``owner/name``), when known: set by
        collection from the producers file, or given on import. Never guessed from names.
PipelineJob.title: PipelineJob

PipelineJobView.description: One job of a pipeline execution: its highest attempt.
PipelineJobView.title: PipelineJobView

PipelineView.description:
One pipeline execution (docs/pipelines.md), with what collection recorded about it.

Attributes:
    status: ``incomplete`` when jobs or reports are missing (whatever the CI concluded),

        ``cancelled`` ...), else ``complete`` for pipelines imported without collection.
PipelineView.title: PipelineView

PipelinesView.description:
Every pipeline execution in scope, newest first, judged against the expected jobs.

Attributes:

schema.title: Response Execution Options Api Execution Options Get

get.description:
Historical test-execution dashboard; counts all reports in scope, not the latest snapshot.

``kind`` (an execution family such as ``api`` or ``ui``) is part of the scope like on every route.
Filter values that exist in the data.
Requirements without automated coverage in priority order, grouped by owner.
The release gate on each day's snapshot (last 30 days with runs) and the days it changed.
Liveness check with the size of the loaded data, the deployed commit and the catalog notice.
Issue drafts for the top recurring failures; drafts only, nothing is created (docs/issues.md).
Pipeline executions, newest first; with ``jobs``, the ones missing a job are incomplete.
Release status of the scope (ready / at risk / blocked / unknown) by the documented policy.
Each suite's newest build against its previous build on the same branch (build filter ignored).
Recorded repository / test type / browser / environment combinations for the filter bar.

schema.title: Response Report Options Api Report Options Get

get.description: The latest snapshot as the report overview: totals, suites, failure causes, trend.
The latest snapshot as a tree: repository (or framework) > job > class > test.
Each repository's snapshot on the newest day with runs against ``days`` earlier.
In-scope requirements, optionally filtered by status, linked result evidence, or staleness.
Requirements in scope by criticality and by feature, with coverage, execution and stale counts.
One requirement with its test cases and their latest executions.
Imported runs, newest first.
One run with all results, failures first.

Everything whose text contains every word of ``q`` (2-100 characters), grouped by kind.

Searched: repositories, workflows, pipelines, tests, requirements and failure messages. Each
group shows at most ``limit`` results and its full count; repository and date filters apply.
Flaky candidates, consistent and new failures, recurring failures, slow-downs, trends.

When the data was loaded, how fresh it is, and the last refresh error.

``check=true`` looks for new data now (at most once every few seconds); the answer
describes the data current after that check.
Coverage metrics, gaps and the execution snapshot.
Every executed test with its counts; ``outcome`` keeps tests whose latest result has it.
All executions of one test, newest first (the key goes in the query: it contains '/').
A copyable summary of one test's investigation, as text and Markdown.
Daily execution snapshots, per-context run series and recorded coverage snapshots.
